caption:
You don't need ten tabs open to know if something's actually true.

Most health or productivity questions turn into the same spiral: a search, a wall of contradicting blog posts, a wellness account with strong opinions and no sources, and one paywalled study you can't finish reading. You close the tabs no smarter than when you opened them.

Consensus is a search engine that only answers using peer-reviewed research — it scans over 200 million papers from places like Semantic Scholar and OpenAlex. Ask it something like "does magnesium help with sleep" and instead of ten opinions, you get a single bar: a Consensus Meter showing how many real studies say yes, no, or mixed.

Ask a bigger question and Pro Search goes further — it writes a plain summary of what's known, shows a timeline of how the research has shifted over the years, names the scientists actually leading the field, and points out what hasn't been studied enough yet. There's also a claims table that rates how strong each individual finding is, with the paper linked right beside it.

One honest catch: the meter counts which way studies lean, not how rigorous each one is — so treat it as where research starts, not where an argument ends.

Still, the next time you catch yourself mid-argument in a comments section about whether something is "actually" backed by science, this is a genuinely different way to check than typing it into Google.

Save this so you don't lose it. Try Consensus on the next thing you've always wondered about — full breakdown, link in bio.
